findings.action: Unresolved R3-F9: shallow histories can meet the 500-commit threshold and consult no Bloom filters, producing a fixable rewrite recommendation, although Git cannot use or write commit-graphs across shallow boundaries. The repair can succeed without resolving the finding, violating R2. Read-only probes confirmed count=500, shallow=true and no Bloom events. Detect shallow history, provide actionable remediation or reconcile the requirement, and add a regression.

Unresolved R3-F10: the repair inherits commitGraph.maxNewFilters. With zero, no new filters are generated; restrictive limits can also leave the probe unaccelerated. Git can return success while doctor remains next, violating R2. Diagnose the effective limit or explicitly override it for this repair, and cover zero and restrictive limits.

Unresolved R3-F11: an empty HEAD tree returns a successful state with filtersUsed=false before probing or checking disabled reads. Above the threshold, doctor therefore recommends rewriting indefinitely, including after a successful repair, and omits disabled-read diagnostics. R2 has no nonempty-tree exclusion. Handle the absence of a probeable path explicitly and add regression coverage.

Unresolved R3-F12: disabled-read detection ignores Git configuration precedence. changedPathsVersion overrides deprecated readChangedPaths, but readChangedPaths=false is checked first. With changedPathsVersion=1 and a missing graph, doctor incorrectly removes the repair and names an ineffective setting as the cause. A read-only probe confirmed filters remain readable under these conflicting settings. Resolve the effective version first and test the missing-graph case.

Unresolved R3-F13: diagnostic Git commands do not disable lazy fetching. In a partial clone, recursive ls-tree or path-history lookup can fetch promised trees and write objects during plain doctor or a fix preview. This violates the read-only constraint and D1's authority boundary. Disable lazy fetching for diagnostics, report unavailable local objects, and test that no remote contact occurs.

Unresolved R3-F14 and remaining R1-F5: stderr is discarded whenever Git exits successfully. Git can report an unreadable or malformed commit-graph, fall back to ordinary traversal and exit zero. Doctor then reports next, or ok below the threshold, instead of R3's bounded operational warning. Preserve and classify graph-read diagnostics on successful commands and add corrupt-graph regression coverage.
